welcome.headline: Turn what's actually happening to you into something you can see.
welcome.body: EMBR helps you turn what you're experiencing into something you can look back on, understand, and eventually bring into a conversation with your doctor. It doesn't diagnose you or replace your clinician. It helps you organize your own record, on your own terms.

jobToBeDone.headline: What do you want EMBR to help you with?
jobToBeDone.hint: This just shapes what we show you first. You can always change your mind later.
jobToBeDone.keepRecord: Keep a better record, long term

whatsGoingOn.headline: What have you noticed lately?
whatsGoingOn.hint: Pick anything that's felt different recently. This is just a starting point. Your first check-in will build from what you notice here.
whatsGoingOn.sleepExamples: Trouble falling asleep · Waking during the night · Night sweats · Waking tired
whatsGoingOn.energyExamples: Lower energy · Sudden tiredness · Needing more rest · Energy changes
whatsGoingOn.moodExamples: Irritability · Feeling emotional · Anxiety · Feeling low · Mood changes
whatsGoingOn.bodyExamples: Hot flashes · Headaches · Aches · Bloating · Skin · Hair · Temperature
whatsGoingOn.focusExamples: Brain fog · Concentration · Forgetfulness · Finding words · Mental fatigue
whatsGoingOn.somethingElseExamples: Digestion · Libido · Vaginal or urinary changes · Stress · Exercise · Treatments

appointmentStatus.headline: Do you have a healthcare appointment coming up?
appointmentStatus.hint: No need for the exact date yet. Just helps us know whether to keep a Clinical Brief close at hand.
appointmentStatus.withinThreeMonthsOrLonger: Within the next 3 months or longer

theLoop.headline: Here's how EMBR works.
theLoop.trackTreatmentsHint: You can also keep track of treatments you try, including HRT, supplements, medication, or anything else you want to remember.
theLoop.patternsTitle: After you've logged for a couple of weeks, EMBR can help you look back at what was happening together.
theLoop.patternsExample: "On 6 days, lower energy appeared alongside disrupted sleep."
theLoop.patternsCaveat: These are patterns in your records, not diagnoses. EMBR does not tell you what is causing your symptoms.
theLoop.briefBody: When you want one, EMBR turns your records into a simple summary you can take to a healthcare appointment.
theLoop.briefControlNote: You decide when to create it. Nothing is generated automatically.
theLoop.conversationTitle: You can use your Brief to help explain what you've been experiencing, what you've noticed over time, and what you want to ask about.
theLoop.conversationBody: You can also just keep using EMBR for yourself.

startingPoint.keepRecord: Let's start building your record over time.
startingPoint.notSure: Let's see what your record starts to show.

Dashboard.recordDescription: Everything you log becomes part of this record.
Dashboard.patternsBody: A weekly view of what's changing. As your record grows, the fuller picture takes shape in Signals.
Dashboard.evidenceBody: Your Clinical Brief turns your recorded history into what you can bring to your GP.

Timeline.title: Timeline
Timeline.subtitle: Every entry in your record, in order.
Timeline.emptyBody: As you log symptoms, cycle days, and treatments, they'll appear here in order, day by day.

Timeline.truncatedNotice: Showing your most recently recorded activity from the last {days} days.

Trends.title: Signals
Trends.subtitle: See what your record is beginning to show over time.
Trends.noSymptomsBody: Start logging to build your record. As your history grows, EMBR will organize your reported symptoms here.
Trends.noCycleDataYet: Add at least two period-start dates to see your recorded cycle lengths here.
Trends.noCycleDataCaveat: Irregular or absent cycles are common in perimenopause. This is a record for you and your provider, not a diagnosis.
Trends.averagingDays: Averaging {days} days between period starts over this window.
Trends.irregularityNote: Cycle irregularity is expected during perimenopause. This view is here to help you notice your own pattern, not to flag it as a problem.

CoOccurrence.cardDescription: What EMBR can surface from your record once there's enough to show a signal.
CoOccurrence.sharedDaysCount: {days, plural, one {# shared day} other {# shared days}}
CoOccurrence.observedText: {categoryA} was logged {countA, plural, one {# time} other {# times}} in the last {days} days. {categoryB} was logged {countB, plural, one {# time} other {# times}}.
CoOccurrence.caveat: A description of what you've logged: not a diagnosis, and not a claim about cause.
CoOccurrence.whyReasoning: EMBR surfaces a signal like this once two symptoms have been recorded together on at least 3 separate days. {categoryA} and {categoryB} currently share {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}.
CoOccurrence.questionText: Is it common for {categoryA} and {categoryB} to occur together at this stage?
CoOccurrence.questionCaveat: A suggested question, not medical advice.
CoOccurrence.emptyTitle: Your record is still taking shape.
CoOccurrence.emptyBody: EMBR needs more observations before it can surface a signal here. Keep logging over time; this section will update as your record grows.

EvidenceStrength.groupLabel: How much of your record exists so far

caption.EARLY: You're building your record. As you log more consistently, EMBR can surface stronger signals across symptoms and time.
caption.EMERGING: Your record is starting to take shape. Keep logging to build a fuller picture.
caption.ESTABLISHED: You have a solid record to draw on.

Organization.title: Organization
Organization.notAMember: You're not part of an organization on EMBR. This page is for the person who administers an employer, insurer, or clinic account.
Organization.notAnAdmin: You belong to an organization, but only its ORG_ADMIN can manage the roster and see aggregate trends. If that should be you, ask your organization's admin to change your role.

Organization.ssoDescription: Let members at your email domain log in through your identity provider instead of a password. Password login keeps working either way. This doesn't replace it.
Organization.trendsAnonymizedNote: Anonymized across your organization: never any one member's individual record.
Organization.trendsSuppressed: Not enough people have logged symptoms in this window yet to show a trend without risking identifying any one person. This isn't about your organization being too small overall. It's about how many members have actually logged something recently.
Organization.trendsEmpty: Nothing logged across the organization in this window yet.

Export.title: Export your data

Export.clinicianSummaryDescription: A short summary formatted for a doctor's visit: symptom frequency, cycle length, treatment history, and the log itself.
Export.symptomLogsDescription: Every symptom entry in the range, one row each, for your own records or another tool.
Export.cycleEntriesDescription: Every cycle entry in the range, one row each.
Export.treatmentsDescription: Every treatment logged in the range, one row each.
